bull.t: Strong recurring growth and expanding platform scale
bull.b: Toast is adding locations while recurring gross profit, ARR and GPV all grow at low-to-mid-20% rates. A larger installed base increases payment volume and software-module opportunities, supporting durable recurring economics and cross-sell potential beyond a single product.

bull.t: Profitability transition is supported by strong cash generation
bull.b: Positive EBIT and net margins, together with $635M of operating cash flow and $576M of free cash flow, show that the profitability inflection is translating into cash. This improves self-funding capacity and gives Toast flexibility to invest through the next growth phase.

bull.t: Debt-free balance sheet provides financial flexibility
bull.b: Effectively zero debt limits interest and refinancing pressure while preserving flexibility to fund product development, market expansion and customer acquisition internally. The stronger balance sheet also gives Toast greater resilience if restaurant activity or payments volumes become less favorable.

bear.b: TTM revenue growth has slowed to about 5.6% from much higher rates in 2021–2023. Slower expansion can reduce operating leverage and makes future growth more dependent on location additions, product attach and payment-volume gains rather than the existing base alone.

bear.t: Hardware costs weigh on integrated-platform margins
bear.b: Hardware and professional-services gross profit was negative and created an 11% drag on recurring gross profit streams. Persistent hardware-cost pressure can dilute the economics of Toast’s integrated offering and offset software margin gains unless mitigation measures remain effective.

bear.t: Strategic inventory build reduced cash conversion
bear.b: Free cash flow fell year over year to $130M in Q2 because Toast intentionally built hardware inventory. Although management expects conversion to improve in H2, working-capital needs can temporarily absorb cash and reduce resources available for reinvestment or other capital allocation.
